title: VI-MMRec: Similarity-Aware Training Cost-free Virtual User-Item Interactions for Multimodal Recommendation

problem.claim: Multimodal recommendation effectiveness is limited by sparse user-item interactions.

gap.claim: Existing models arbitrarily treat unobserved items as negative samples because users interact with only a small subset of available items.

contributions.claim: A model-agnostic, training cost-free framework enriches sparse interactions with similarity-aware virtual user-item interactions.
The framework provides Overlay and Synergistic strategies to preserve modality-specific preferences and capture complementary cross-modal preferences.
A statistically informed mechanism adaptively assigns virtual-interaction weights according to dataset-specific modality relevance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validation through experiments on six real-world datasets and seven state-of-the-art multimodal recommendation models.
The authors report that VI-MMRec integrates with existing models without modifying their core architecture.
The authors report no additional training overhead and minimal implementation effort.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal recommendation is constrained by sparse user-item interactions and negative treatment of unobserved items.
VI-MMRec augments sparse interactions with virtual interactions derived from modality-specific similarities.
Overlay and Synergistic strategies model modality-specific and complementary cross-modal preferences, while adaptive weighting uses modality relevance.
The framework is presented as plug-and-play, architecture-preserving, and training-overhead-free.
The authors report experiments across six real-world datasets and seven multimodal recommendation models.

source_observation.claim: Virtual interactions are constructed from modality-specific feature similarities of items already interacted with by users.

interpretation.claim: Similarity-based augmentation can expand sparse interaction data while retaining modality-related preference signals.

application.claim: Use similarity-aware virtual interactions as a lightweight augmentation layer for sparse multimodal recommendation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers to domains, modalities, or sparsity patterns beyond the reported setting.

unknowns: The six datasets and seven models are not identified.
No experimental metrics, numerical results, or baselines are provided.
The statistical weight-allocation mechanism is not specified.
The abstract does not report computational measurements supporting the training-overhead claim.
